title: EVM Semantics
description: Defines the Ethereum Virtual Machine's exact execution rules - stack, memory, storage, opcodes - so every node computes identical results. Precise semantics are what make smart contracts deterministic across thousands of independent machines.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Gas Metering
description: Charges per operation so computation has a price, which bounds execution and prevents infinite loops from halting the network. Gas metering aligns incentives: users pay for the resources they consume.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Deterministic Execution
description: Forbids randomness, wall-clock time, and other nondeterminism inside contracts so all nodes agree on outcomes. Determinism is the foundation the whole trust model stands on.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: State Tries
description: Stores contract state in a Merkle-Patricia trie so any state value comes with a compact proof of correctness. Tries let light clients verify contract state without storing everything.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Contract Verification
description: Matches deployed bytecode to published source so users can read the actual code their money interacts with. Verified contracts are the minimum bar for trust: unverified code should be treated as hostile.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Reentrancy Guards
description: Blocks reentrant calls - where a contract is called back mid-execution - the attack behind history's biggest contract hacks. Guards are simple mutexes; skipping them has cost billions.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Upgrade Proxies
description: Separates contract logic from storage behind a proxy so logic can be upgraded while state persists. Proxies enable fixing bugs, but they concentrate trust in whoever holds the upgrade key.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Event Logs
description: Emits structured events during execution that off-chain systems index for history and analytics. Logs are the contract's voice to the outside world - cheap, permanent, and queryable.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Formal Verification
description: Proves contract properties mathematically - 'funds can never be locked', 'only the owner withdraws' - with proof assistants. Verification is the strongest assurance available, reserved for contracts holding serious value.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Fuzzing
description: Bombards contracts with random and mutated inputs hunting for crashes and invariant violations. Fuzzing finds the edge cases human reviewers miss, especially in complex state machines.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Audit Trails
description: Records every contract interaction immutably on-chain, creating a complete auditable history. On-chain trails mean disputes resolve from evidence, not testimony.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Cross-Chain Calls
description: Invokes contracts on other chains through bridges and messaging protocols, composing applications across ecosystems. Cross-chain calls extend reach but inherit bridge risk.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Oracle Integration
description: Feeds real-world data - prices, weather, scores - into contracts through oracle networks with aggregation and dispute handling. Oracles are the bridge between deterministic contracts and a messy world.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Access Control
description: Restricts sensitive functions to authorized roles - owner, minter, pauser - enforced on-chain. Proper access control is the difference between an administered protocol and an exploited one.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Deployment Pipelines
description: Deploys contracts through staged pipelines - testnet, audit, timelocked mainnet - with verification at each gate. Pipelines bring software-engineering discipline to immutable deployments.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
